<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

MEASURED ON PROD 2026-09-02 (assets/inputs/db-cpu-profile-report.md §5, §8 cause #1): the search nearest CTE in crates/store/src/embeddings.rs:557-620 admits a candidate vector with `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM elements admitted WHERE (raw) OR (source_kind='smart' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM smart_content candidate WHERE candidate.text_hash = e.source_hash AND candidate.raw_hash = admitted.raw_hash)))`. Postgres plans that as a Nested Loop Semi Join over a spilling Materialize of a Seq Scan on elements (86,191 rows, rescanned per candidate), producing 962,792–1,698,017 smart_content_text_hash_idx probes and 3.8–6.8M buffer hits PER SEARCH, 1.7–2.7 s each — while the HNSW scan that supposedly dominates takes 12.4 ms / 1,078 buffers. The candidate-expansion loop (MAX_CANDIDATE_EXPANSIONS=8, growth ×2) re-runs the whole query up to 9 times when a pass under-fills: that is the 13 s / 60 s / 120 s searches two coders and a reviewer hit today (row 122). 69% of ALL database CPU in the profiling window; smart_content_text_hash_idx measured at 124,551 scans/s. JIT adds 281 ms/query compiling 88 functions on a cost estimate of 478,936,610. 99.7% buffer hit rate — this is CPU-bound on a bad plan, NOT I/O-bound on shared_buffers (row 122's original premise, falsified by EXPLAIN). Full plan: assets/inputs/db-cpu-profile-report.md and dbprof/explain160.out in governance scratch.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- A search performs O(candidates) work, not O(candidates × elements): the admission predicate is resolved as hash semi-joins (smart_content text_hash→raw_hash resolved ONCE, elements admitted ONCE), never as a correlated per-candidate EXISTS.
- EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) of the shipped query on prod's corpus shows the smart_content probe with loops < 1,000 and total shared buffer hits under 100,000 for limit=40 / candidate_limit=160 (was 962,792 loops / 3.85M hits).
- Ranking parity: the existing search fixtures and the 009 chunk-collapse tests pass unchanged; a new parity test asserts the same top-N addresses and scores (within float tolerance) for the fixture corpus before and after.
- Search wall time on prod for the profile's reference query drops from 1.65 s (single pass) to under 300 ms, and a bare `flowspace3 search` from the main checkout completes under 1 s at idle load. Measured, not estimated.
- The candidate_vectors CTE already carries (source_hash, source_kind, chunk_no, distance) only; the EXPLAIN-shape test now asserts that its target list has no vector column. JIT no longer triggers on this query (cost estimate sane), or is explicitly disabled for it with a stated reason.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- No change to the 009 element collapse semantics, chunk_no handling, or the scoring formula.
- No change to shared_buffers or any postgres config (row 140, separate, needs a restart).
- No change to candidate-expansion policy beyond what parity requires — if the loop still re-runs, it re-runs a cheap query.
- No index additions without a stop-and-ask naming the size and the write cost.
